executive_summary: me-domain Active Directory environment DOMAIN-1 has a critical security posture scoring 1/100, leaving Tier 0 assets at immediate risk of compromise. Multiple low-complexity attack vectors exist, including domain controller vulnerabilities such as missing noPac updates and unenforced Netlogon secure channels, combined with active AD CS misconfigurations (ESC1, ESC2, ESC13) allowing unauthenticated or domain-user level elevation to Domain Admin. Critical identity hygiene issues include exposed SYSVOL passwords, cleartext credentials, writable NETLOGON shares, and non-default DCSync/AdminSDHolder control rights held by standard accounts. Immediate remediation must focus on securing Active Directory Certificate Services, patching core domain controllers, revoking unauthorized domain rights, and rotating stale privileged credentials.

remediation_plan.title: Remediate AD CS Escalation Paths (ESC1, ESC2, ESC13)
remediation_plan.rationale: Breaks instant privilege escalation paths from any domain user to Tier 0 identity certificate issuance.
remediation_plan.caveats: Ensure legitimate PKI clients are identified before removing requester-supplied subject flags or broad enrollment rights.

remediation_plan.title: Patch Domain Controllers and Enforce RPC Security Controls
remediation_plan.rationale: Mitigates direct DC takeovers (noPac, ZeroLogon) and RPC coercion vectors.
remediation_plan.caveats: Requires domain controller OS updates and service restarts; test RPC dependencies for legacy services prior to strict enforcement.

remediation_plan.title: Revoke Unauthorized Tier 0 ACLs and DCSync Privileges
remediation_plan.rationale: Eliminates direct persistence and control points over Domain Controllers and AdminSDHolder.
remediation_plan.caveats: Verify Exchange hybrid and synchronization service account requirements before stripping write rights.

remediation_plan.title: Clean Up Credentials in SYSVOL, GPOs, and Accounts
remediation_plan.rationale: Removes plain-text credential exposures accessible to all domain users.
remediation_plan.caveats: Changing SYSVOL script access may impact non-standard deployment scripts; audit network drive mappings.

remediation_plan.title: Rotate Privileged Credentials and Enforce Account Protection
remediation_plan.rationale: Stops offline credential cracking attacks (Kerberoasting/AS-REP Roasting) and golden ticket persistence.
remediation_plan.caveats: Rotate krbtgt password twice over 24-48 hours; verify service availability for SPN accounts after password changes.

quick_wins: Disable user-supplied subject names (ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT) on certificate template TEMPLATE-1.
Remove write permissions for 'Domain Users' on the NETLOGON share folder PATH-2.
Enforce mandatory password requirement and reset credentials for account USER-22.
Set RequireStrongKey = 1 to enforce Netlogon secure channel protection on Domain Controllers.
Disable AlwaysInstallElevated policy setting in the Default Domain Policy GPO.

monitoring.guidance: Monitor for Directory Service access requests containing DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All (GUID 1131f6ad-9c4d-11d1-bf6d-00c04fd7d5a0) originating from non-DC accounts like USER-31.
Alert on certificate enrollment requests against TEMPLATE-1 or TEMPLATE-3 where Subject Alternative Name (SAN) modifications are submitted by non-administrative users.
Detect machine account creation or modification events where sAMAccountName is altered to mimic a Domain Controller without trailing dollar signs.

attack_paths.title: Domain Escalation via AD CS ESC1 Template
steps: NETBIOS-1\Domain Users -> Request certificate from TEMPLATE-1 supplying Domain Admin SAN
TEMPLATE-1 -> Authenticate as Domain Admin to Tier 0
attack_paths.narrative: Any domain user can request a client authentication certificate matching high-privileged identities, yielding full domain takeover. Modify TEMPLATE-1 to disallow enrollee-supplied subjects.

attack_paths.title: Direct Domain Takeover via Non-Default DCSync Rights
steps: USER-31 -> Replicate AD secrets via DCSync
Tier 0 -> Full domain compromise via hash extraction
attack_paths.narrative: USER-31 possesses ExtendedRight DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All on the domain root, enabling full extraction of domain credentials. Revoke DCSync rights from USER-31.

attack_paths.title: Privilege Escalation via Constrained Delegation with Protocol Transition
steps: USER-18 -> Perform protocol transition (S4U2Self/S4U2Proxy) to cifs/DCHOST-1
cifs/DCHOST-1 -> Impersonate arbitrary privileged user on DC
attack_paths.narrative: USER-18 is configured with protocol transition targeting domain controller services, allowing arbitrary account impersonation against DCHOST-1. Remove protocol transition rights from USER-18.

attack_paths.title: Domain Controller Takeover via noPac Vulnerability
steps: Any Domain User -> Create computer account using MachineAccountQuota
Computer Account -> Rename sAMAccountName to match DCHOST-2 without '$'
DCHOST-2 -> Request TGT and exploit missing noPac patch to obtain Domain Admin TGT
attack_paths.narrative: Unpatched DC DCHOST-2 coupled with non-zero MachineAccountQuota permits unprivileged users to request DC-privileged tickets. Apply the noPac patch to DCHOST-2.

attack_paths.title: Domain Takeover via Unconstrained Delegation Computer Account
steps: HOST-2$ -> Coerce authentication from a Domain Controller to HOST-2$
HOST-2$ -> Extract cached DC TGT from LSASS memory to compromise Tier 0
attack_paths.narrative: HOST-2$ is configured with unconstrained delegation, permitting extraction of administrative TGTs upon authentication. Remove TRUSTED_FOR_DELEGATION from HOST-2$.

remediation_scripts.caveats: Ensure target template object name matches and test application authentication flow post-update.
May break automated domain-join processes relying on non-administrative user credentials.
Coordinate credential updates with account owners.

triage.rationale: Allows any standard user immediate elevation to full Domain Admin via certificate SAN injection.
Grants direct execution of DCSync replication to extract all domain password hashes.
Provides a reliable privilege escalation path to DC host compromise from any authenticated account.
Enables arbitrary user impersonation against CIFS services on domain controllers.
Allows authenticated attackers to modify domain-wide logon scripts for widespread code execution.

known_exploitation.public: Widely reported in ransomware and advanced threat actor intrusions (Certified Pre-Owned research).
known_exploitation.relevance: TEMPLATE-1 allows Domain Users to supply arbitrary subject names with client authentication.

known_exploitation.public: Actively exploited across enterprise environments post-disclosure.
known_exploitation.relevance: DCHOST-2 is missing build patches while Machine Account Quota is set to 10.

known_exploitation.public: Widely documented and integrated into automated attack frameworks.
known_exploitation.relevance: Domain Controllers lack enforced secure channel protection.

compromise_assessment.summary: The environment presents trivial path combinations allowing low-privileged domain users to achieve complete Tier 0 domain takeover. Exposure across AD CS configuration, unpatched domain controllers, and excess replication rights ensures high attack chain reliability.

chains.title: Standard Domain User to Domain Admin via AD CS ESC1

break_point.why: Disabling ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT or restricting enrollment rights stops unauthorized identity impersonation.

chains.narrative: An authenticated low-privileged account requests a certificate using TEMPLATE-1 specifying a Domain Admin sAMAccountName, immediately receiving full administrative privileges.

chains.title: Account USER-31 Direct DCSync Replication

break_point.why: Revoking DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All from USER-31 removes secret replication privileges.

chains.narrative: Control over USER-31 enables immediate execution of DCSync against the domain head to pull all domain account hashes, granting full control.

rejected_chains.title: Coercion to WebDAV Relay via Disabled WebClient
rejected_chains.reason: WebClient service is running on DCHOST-2; chain was evaluated as viable rather than rejected.
